questions.question:
The Pod `rogue-pod` runs in the namespace `forensics-lab` on the worker node `{{NODE01}}`. Its container `snooper-container` keeps reading a sensitive file named `secret.txt`. Falco is installed on `{{NODE01}}`.

Write a custom Falco rule in `/tmp/exam/mhagou-008-q1/catch-rogue.yaml` (on the jumphost, or on `{{NODE01}}` if you work there). The file must be self-contained: Falco must run with `falco -r /tmp/exam/mhagou-008-q1/catch-rogue.yaml` on `{{NODE01}}`.

The rule must detect when a process **inside a container** reads `secret.txt`. The alert it produces must show:

- the container that accessed the file (its id or its name);
- the path of the file;
- the command that read it.

Reads of the same file made directly on the host must **not** trigger the rule. Do not modify or restart `rogue-pod`.

verification.description: Falco loads the rule file /tmp/exam/mhagou-008-q1/catch-rogue.yaml and runs with it
The rule raises an alert when the container reads secret.txt
The alert identifies the container (id or name)
The alert shows the file path and the command that read the file
Reads of secret.txt made on the host do not trigger the rule
Ingress secure-ingress (class traefik) routes secure-app.company.com / to Service secure-app with TLS from web-tls
https://secure-app.company.com/ returns the page of secure-app
The certificate of web-tls is served for secure-app.company.com
HTTP requests for secure-app.company.com are redirected to HTTPS
block-malicious-egress selects all Pods of threat-prevention and restricts egress only
DNS over UDP/53 and TCP/53 is allowed to any destination
The two malicious /24 ranges are blocked and all other egress traffic is allowed
With the policy in force DNS names resolve from the Pods

questions.question:
The ServiceAccount `ci-bot` in the namespace `ci-cd` has more permissions than it needs: they allow it to give itself cluster-admin rights.

Change the RBAC configuration so that:

- `ci-bot` cannot bind itself to any role whose name contains `admin` or `cluster-admin`, neither with a ClusterRoleBinding nor with a RoleBinding;
- `ci-bot` keeps its current permissions on workloads in `ci-cd` (pods, services, configmaps, deployments, replicasets) and its read-only access to rolebindings and clusterrolebindings.

The permissions are granted through the ClusterRole `ci-bot-role` and the ClusterRoleBinding `ci-bot-binding`. Recreate objects if you need to (the `roleRef` of a binding cannot be changed).

verification.description: ci-bot cannot bind itself to cluster-admin (ClusterRoleBinding or RoleBinding)
ci-bot cannot bind itself to admin (ClusterRoleBinding or RoleBinding)
ci-bot keeps its permissions on pods, services and configmaps in ci-cd
ci-bot keeps its permissions on deployments and replicasets in ci-cd
ci-bot can still read rolebindings and clusterrolebindings
The base image is gcr.io/distroless/base
Only FROM, COPY (app-server to /app/server), USER and ENTRYPOINT remain
The container runs as the non-root user nonroot / 65532
/app/server is the ENTRYPOINT in exec form

questions.question:
A security audit found that containers in the namespace `secure-runtime` can be used for process debugging attacks. The Pod `secure-app` runs in the namespace on the worker node `{{NODE01}}`.

1. Create a custom seccomp profile that blocks the syscalls `ptrace` and `process_vm_readv` with the action `SCMP_ACT_ERRNO` and allows all the other syscalls (default action `SCMP_ACT_ALLOW`).
2. Save it as `/var/lib/kubelet/seccomp/profiles/block-debug.json` on `{{NODE01}}`.
3. Make `secure-app` use the profile (a seccomp profile cannot be changed in a running Pod: re-create the Pod, keep its name, namespace and node).
4. The Pod must stay functional: Running, Ready, and answering on port 80.

verification.description: A valid profile exists at /var/lib/kubelet/seccomp/profiles/block-debug.json on {{NODE01}}
The profile allows everything except ptrace and process_vm_readv (SCMP_ACT_ERRNO)
secure-app uses the Localhost profile, is Running and Ready and answers on port 80
A seccomp filter is active in every container of secure-app
